TYP-001: Customer engages in activity consistent with 'Investment/Ponzi crypto fraud' that is not adequately detected because the following indicator(s) do not fire: Credentials or identifiers shared with another account; Forged or edited identification documents; Sender unfamiliar with VA technology or custodial wallets; Crypto-to-plastic conversion or cash-funded credit cards; Non-hosted / self-custody wallet with attribution risk; AI-orchestrated synthetic-identity impersonation at onboarding. Draft indicator: assess transactions exhibiting fake trading platform, promised returns, withdrawal block, currently outside explicit coverage of the existing rulebook.
TYP-006: A customer is exhibiting suspicious activity in their account by consistently structuring transactions into smaller, less frequent amounts, or into multiple accounts, or by failing to report the origin of a large or unusual transaction.
TYP-004: A "Customer is attempting to initiate a transaction using a voice clone or phishing call, or is using a cloned mobile application, and has provided sensitive information, such as login credentials or account numbers, in response."
TYP-008: A candidate's ability to create, manipulate, or alter digital content in a way that deceives or misleads others, potentially to facilitate financial crimes, should be thoroughly assessed and monitored.
TYP-005: "Compliance team should watch for suspicious transactions involving rapid volume, new account opening, and synthetic identity indicators, such as unusual login activity or large transfers from a single IP address."
TYP-003: A financial institution's customer is opening a new, unregistered, high-value account in a foreign jurisdiction with a fresh wallet, and is making multiple transactions through a series of pass-through accounts, without providing any clear business or financial purpose.
TYP-002: A candidate's use of deepfake personas, deepfake media, synthetic identities, or social engineering tactics in their transactions or communications may indicate an attempt to conceal their true identity or facilitate financial crimes.
TYP-007: Customer engages in activity consistent with 'Romance scam with AI deepfake video persona' that is not adequately detected because the following indicator(s) do not fire: Rapid accumulation then off-boarding of value; AI-orchestrated synthetic-identity impersonation at onboarding. Draft indicator: assess transactions exhibiting ai persona, deepfake persona, deepfake media, currently outside explicit coverage of the existing rulebook.
TYP-009: A user's account has been accessed from an unfamiliar location or device, or their login credentials have been shared with another account.
TYP-010: A "Suspicious Transaction Indicator: Unusual Non-Entity Ownership (ubo) or Legal Person Account Activity."
TYP-011: "Compliance team should watch for suspicious transactions involving unverified or unstructured non-identified entities, beneficial ownership structures that lack clear or unexplained relationships, and entities with multiple layers of legal persons or complex ownership arrangements."
TYP-012: We will be monitoring for suspicious activity in transactions involving large, unstructured funds, multiple senders, and small, unverified recipient wallets.
TYP-013: A financial institution should be aware of suspicious activity that involves a series of transactions or account movements that appear to be part of a larger, complex scheme, including transactions that involve multiple parties, multiple locations, and multiple currencies.
TYP-014: A candidate's account is at risk if they exhibit unusual patterns of cross-chain transactions, frequent or large chain hops, or suspicious layering activities.
TYP-015: Customer engages in activity consistent with 'Mixer-assisted sanitisation' that is not adequately detected because the following indicator(s) do not fire: Repeated transactions with a subset of individuals; Intermediate (tier-2) tokens or convertible currencies; Round or structured amounts with no rationale. Draft indicator: assess transactions exhibiting mixer, tumbler, sanitisation, currently outside explicit coverage of the existing rulebook.
TYP-016: A "Customer has recently purchased a privacy coin or has shown interest in a convertible or token swap, and has not provided any clear explanation for their transactions or has been hesitant to disclose their wallet information."
TYP-017: Customer engages in activity consistent with 'Ransomware payment facilitation' that is not adequately detected because the following indicator(s) do not fire: Funds sourced from mixing services or tumbler wallets; Transfers to/from an exchange not registered in the jurisdiction; Sanctions / targeted financial sanctions screening; Use of anonymity-enhancing technologies (VPN/Tor). Draft indicator: assess transactions exhibiting ransomware, extortion, darknet, currently outside explicit coverage of the existing rulebook.
TYP-018: Customer engages in activity consistent with 'Sextortion / financial-release extortion' that is not adequately detected because the following indicator(s) do not fire: Funds sourced from mixing services or tumbler wallets; Use of anonymity-enhancing technologies (VPN/Tor); Suspicious-beneficiary VA wallet with little history; Coached mule / scam-victim behaviour pattern. Draft indicator: assess transactions exhibiting extortion, darknet, memo field, currently outside explicit coverage of the existing rulebook.
TYP-019: A candidate's use of high-pressure sales tactics, unusually large or frequent transactions, or unexplained changes in their account activity may indicate a social engineering or voice clone scam.
TYP-020: A financial institution should be aware of customers who consistently deposit small amounts of cash in a short period, or who make multiple deposits of less than $10,000 in a single transaction.
TYP-021: A financial institution should be aware of customers exhibiting suspicious behavior that may indicate they are attempting to layer or obfuscate transactions, particularly if they are doing so across multiple accounts or in a manner that is not typical for their transactional patterns.
TYP-022: A suspicious pattern of withdrawal from a large number of accounts, with a round number, and a withdrawal amount that is a multiple of a significant portion of the account balance.
TYP-023: A candidate's high volume of cross-border wire transfers from a single, unverified account in a low-risk country to multiple, high-risk countries, or their high velocity, may indicate a potential money laundering scheme.
TYP-024: A suspicious pattern of multiple small transactions across different accounts, particularly if occurring in a short period, may indicate wash trading activity.
TYP-025: Customer engages in activity consistent with 'Fresh-wallet mule factory' that is not adequately detected because the following indicator(s) do not fire: Sender unfamiliar with VA technology or custodial wallets; Use of anonymity-enhancing technologies (VPN/Tor). Draft indicator: assess transactions exhibiting fresh wallet, new wallet, no history, currently outside explicit coverage of the existing rulebook.
TYP-026: A "Customer Account Change Indicator" should be triggered when an account holder's account details, such as login credentials or email address, are modified without the prior consent of the account owner or in a manner that raises suspicions of unauthorized access or manipulation.
TYP-027: A suspicious combination of a customer's relocation to a high-risk jurisdiction, unlicensed activity in a jurisdiction not registered with the regulator, and unregistered exchange activity.
TYP-028: A customer's frequent international transfers to unknown destinations, or those exceeding $50,000 in a single transaction, may indicate suspicious activity.
TYP-029: Customer engages in activity consistent with 'Sanctioned-entity wallet interop' that is not adequately detected because the following indicator(s) do not fire: Sender unfamiliar with VA technology or custodial wallets; Transactions with addresses connected to criminal schemes; Transfers to/from an exchange not registered in the jurisdiction; Sanctions / targeted financial sanctions screening. Draft indicator: assess transactions exhibiting sanctions, screening, freeze, currently outside explicit coverage of the existing rulebook.
TYP-030: "Compliance team should watch for suspicious transactions involving high-risk darknet marketplaces, individuals with a history of organized crime involvement, stolen or compromised payment card numbers, and entities with publicly available threat intelligence indicating malicious activity."
TYP-031: We will be monitoring for suspicious patterns of large cash transactions, unusual account activity, and clients who require enhanced due diligence.
TYP-032: Customer engages in activity consistent with 'Unregistered P2P arbitrage cash-out' that is not adequately detected because the following indicator(s) do not fire: Offices in unregulated or no-rationale jurisdictions; Rapid accumulation then off-boarding of value; Round or structured amounts with no rationale. Draft indicator: assess transactions exhibiting p2p, unregistered exchange, crypto to plastic, currently outside explicit coverage of the existing rulebook.
TYP-033: Customer engages in activity consistent with 'Fresh-wallet AI-coached mule victims' that is not adequately detected because the following indicator(s) do not fire: AI-orchestrated synthetic-identity impersonation at onboarding. Draft indicator: assess transactions exhibiting coached, limited literacy, victim, currently outside explicit coverage of the existing rulebook.
TYP-034: Customer engages in activity consistent with 'LLM-generated bulk phishing / mass ATO' that is not adequately detected because the following indicator(s) do not fire: Sender unfamiliar with VA technology or custodial wallets; Use of anonymity-enhancing technologies (VPN/Tor). Draft indicator: assess transactions exhibiting phishing, account takeover, changed credentials, currently outside explicit coverage of the existing rulebook.
TYP-035: A candidate's ability to identify and report suspicious social engineering activities, such as requests for sensitive information or urgent transactions, where the originator's identity or location is unclear or inconsistent.
